title: Moving Beyond AI-Assisted Design – Agentrys Shows the Way with Agentic Loop Engineering
gist: Agentrys says its Studio platform used 'agentic loop engineering' — coupled microarchitecture and RTL optimization loops grounded in real synthesis/P&R measurements — to find a XiangShan RISC-V configuration with 40% higher throughput, 28% lower power and 10% less area than an expert-tuned reference in eight hours with about 50 physical evaluations, while meeting a 1.5 GHz target the reference missed. The piece, a vendor case-study summary, also cites OpenAI's Jalapeño inference ASIC at Hot Chips 2026 as a loop-engineering example.

insights.claim: At Hot Chips 2026, OpenAI presented Jalapeño, an inference ASIC built with AI in the design loop, showing a 56% block-level win on a BF16 multiply and a 10% smaller matrix-unit area versus a human baseline within roughly nine months from RTL to tapeout (as reported by ServeTheHome and Tom's Hardware).
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler/AI-lab in-house ASICs are using AI-in-the-loop design to compress schedules — pressure on traditional EDA workflows.

insights.claim: Loop engineering is defined as designing the objectives, actions, evaluators, state and failure-handling mechanisms that connect each design result to the next design change.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Value in AI chip design shifts to the orchestration/evaluator layer rather than single-task copilots.
insights.quote: designing the objectives, actions, evaluators, state, and failure-handling mechanisms that connect each result to the next design change

insights.claim: Agentrys' workflow found a XiangShan RISC-V configuration in eight hours that improved throughput by 40%, cut power by 28% and reduced area by 10% relative to an expert-tuned reference design.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: If generalizable, autonomous PPA exploration could materially cut design cost and time-to-tapeout.
insights.locator: Agentrys has applied this approach to XiangShan

insights.claim: The optimized configuration met a 1.5 GHz timing objective that the reference configuration could not meet, and another Pareto point achieved about 0.84 W and 0.134 mm² at 1.5 GHz by trading some throughput.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Delivering a Pareto frontier rather than one answer fits how product teams choose SKUs.

insights.claim: Results will vary across workloads, technologies and architectures; the demonstration was on one workload (GAP BFS) using an open-source ASIC implementation environment.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Headline gains are workload-specific; discount before extrapolating to commercial designs and tools.
insights.locator: While results will vary across workloads

insights.claim: XiangShan comprises about 143,000 lines of Chisel across 528 source files with 3,284 adjustable parameters in 17 microarchitectural subsystems, making manual exploration impractical.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Parameter-space scale is the argument for agentic exploration over human trial-and-error.

insights.claim: Because about 88% of GAP BFS execution cycles were memory stalls, processor structures contributing little to that workload could be shrunk or redesigned to save power and area — the source of much of the PPA gain.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Workload-specific de-featuring is a major lever; implies large gains for custom accelerators tuned to narrow workloads.
insights.locator: The primary benchmark was GAP BFS

themes.theme: Two coupled loops grounded in physical results

insights.claim: Agentrys uses an outer loop that optimizes microarchitecture (pipeline widths, caches, queue depths, register files) with dimensionality reduction and predictive models, and an inner loop that optimizes RTL via switching-activity analysis and transforms such as clock gating, operand isolation, retiming and logic removal; the loops cooperate and learn across evaluations.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Combining architecture search with RTL-level power transforms is the differentiated technical claim.

insights.claim: Final decisions are grounded in implementation measurements — compilation, correctness checks, cycle-accurate simulation, synthesis, place-and-route, timing and power analysis — rather than model predictions, because architecturally attractive designs can fail timing after implementation.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Agentic design tools still depend on EDA tool runs — demand for EDA compute/licenses may rise, not fall.
insights.locator: Physical Results, Not Just AI Predictions

insights.claim: Roughly 50 physical evaluations were enough for the system to explore the design space and find a significantly improved set of alternatives.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Low evaluation count suggests predictive pruning makes the approach compute-affordable.

insights.claim: Agentrys Studio separates orchestration from architecture, workloads, design tools and targets so it can incorporate proprietary RTL, commercial EDA tools, internal scripts and specialized agents, and is designed to support other toolchains and FPGA targets.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Tool-agnostic orchestration positions Agentrys as a layer above incumbents rather than a replacement.

insights.claim: Engineering effort will shift from repetitive trial-and-error optimization toward defining objectives, constraints, evaluation methods and architectural priorities, with autonomous agents exploring how to achieve them.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Changes the skill mix and headcount economics of chip design teams.
insights.quote: Engineers establish what the design must accomplish. Autonomous agents explore how best to accomplish it.

insights.claim: AI's greatest contribution to chip design may come from orchestrating and continuously improving the whole optimization process rather than from individual design recommendations.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Point-tool copilots may be commoditized; closed-loop orchestration is where value accrues.
insights.locator: While results will vary across workloads
